free_tier.stated: Co-funding of up to SGD 150,000 per project, with a dedicated AI Engineering Hub of full-time AI, data and platform engineers building and deploying an AI minimum viable product over 6 months; a newer 100E 3-month proof-of-concept path runs with 2 to 3 AI engineers. Organisations must match the funding with in-kind manpower and cash.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: Because the deliverable is engineers rather than credits, 100E does not compose with a cloud free tier in the usual way: the compute sits inside AI Singapore's own environment, so the only thing the client takes away is the model and the code, not a billing account.

limits.value: The award is co-funding against a Singapore organisation's own cash and manpower contribution, delivered by an AI Singapore engineering team, so an applicant has to be an established organisation with staff to second and money to match.

limits_note: The award is co-funding against a Singapore organisation's own cash and manpower contribution, delivered by an AI Singapore engineering team, so an applicant has to be an established organisation with staff to second and money to match.
binding_note: The award is co-funding against a Singapore organisation's own cash and manpower contribution, delivered by an AI Singapore engineering team, so an applicant has to be an established organisation with staff to second and money to match.

evidence.proved: the 100E programme 'provides co-funding of up to SGD$150,000 per project'; 'Organisations are required to match this funding with in-kind contribution (manpower) and cash', quoted

the MVP path runs 'over 6 months' with 'a dedicated AI Engineering Hub (AIEH), comprising full-time AI, data, and platform engineers'; the 3-month POC path uses '2 - 3 AI Engineers & Project Manager', quoted

'The total cash (including the Indirect Research Costs and GST) to be paid will be invoiced to the organisation upon the endorsement of the Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA) for the project', quoted

notes: The SGD 150,000 is a co-funding ceiling, not a grant, and the cash share is invoiced up front against a signed Research Collaboration Agreement, which inverts the cash flow a grant applicant expects. Three readings were considered. (a) An individual can apply: refuted, the unit is an organisation and the contract is with it. (b) The 3-month POC path is cheaper: plausible, the page says 'Lower Commitment' without a figure, so the amount is null here rather than assumed to be half. (c) The Singapore gate is nationality: unresolved, the page read names organisations without stating a registration or residency test, and the strict requirement may sit in the application form, which was not read.
